title: Charm City Kings — HBO Max AR Face Filters
subtitle: XR · AR · Brand Campaign
blurb: A 2-week Spark AR filter campaign for HBO Max's Charm City Kings — 'They call me…' face filters that turn fans into the movie's Baltimore nicknames.
description: For the release of Charm City Kings, HBO Max wanted a way to put fans inside the film's dirt-bike world directly from their phone cameras — no app, no download. The filter turns a marketing beat into something a fan can step into and share.

details.challenge: Standard promo assets ask an audience to sit back; HBO Max wanted something a fan could step inside and share — a moment of participation instead of a passive trailer view.
details.approach: Pulled visual language from the film's dirt-bike and Baltimore street culture, built the AR triggers and overlays in Spark AR and Blender, aligned type and metrics to HBO Max's campaign guidelines, then cross-device tested and submitted to Instagram and Facebook.
details.result: Shipped as an official HBO Max campaign filter for Charm City Kings, live on Instagram and Facebook — turning a passive trailer moment into a participatory brand touchpoint.

imageAlt: They call me Holy Savage — Charm City Kings AR face filter frame

process.name: Concept & Mood
process.body: Pulled visual language from the film's dirt-bike and Baltimore street culture.

process.body: Built the AR triggers and overlays in Spark AR and Blender.

process.body: Aligned type and metrics to HBO Max's campaign guidelines.

process.name: Test & Publish
process.body: Cross-device testing, then submission to Instagram and Facebook.

quote: A filter lives or dies in the first half second — the challenge wasn't the AR technology, it was making the film's world recognizable instantly, in a format most people scroll straight past.

title: Immersive VR Training for Fiber Optic Technicians
subtitle: XR · Enterprise
blurb: VR fiber-optic field training deployed via ArborXR, published on the Meta Quest Store — a fail-safe place to learn splicing and fault diagnosis.
description: Millennium needed field technicians trained on fiber-optic splicing and fault diagnosis without pulling them off paying jobs or risking live customer equipment. The Broken Mile puts them inside a full VR fiber cabinet to run a real troubleshooting job start to finish, as many times as it takes. Deployed via ArborXR and published on the Meta Quest Store.

details.challenge: You can't practice on a live line. Field techs learned splicing by shadowing senior technicians and by trial and error on real customer equipment — expensive when it went wrong, and inconsistent as a way to build judgment.
details.approach: Shadowed field technicians to map the real troubleshooting sequence, then built the fiber cabinet and hand-tracked splice interactions, layered guided and free-play modes so skills build in stages, and packaged the result for ArborXR fleet management.
details.result: Published on the Meta Quest Store and deployed via ArborXR to Millennium's field technician onboarding — replacing live-equipment shadowing with a repeatable, fail-safe practice environment.

notes_wireframe.reflection: Designing for safety-critical, hands-on skills meant the interactive fidelity had to feel like the real tool, not a simplified stand-in — every splice, every fault, had to be trustworthy enough that the learning actually transferred to the field.

details.challenge: 3D on the web often feels gimmicky — latency, missing affordance, and heavy assets break presence and make it feel bolted-on.
details.approach: Prototyped real-time 3D environments, iterating on spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion to keep everything responsive and performant in the browser.
details.result: A set of reusable spatial interaction patterns for interactive 3D that feel native — turning 3D from a novelty into a usable medium.
